findings.claim: Generated code is not excluded from coverage on netstandard2.0/.NET Framework targets. This looks like a gap against 'all generated code', but ledger L7 records that the team has no preference and says to follow the requirement, so the change's guard is a recorded non-defect.

receipt_plan.detail: [L7] Q: should netstandard2.0/.NET Framework generated code also be excluded? A: No preference; follow the requirement. The #if !NETSTANDARD2_0 && !NETFRAMEWORK guard is acceptable.

findings.claim: The README states that all generated formatters and resolvers are decorated, but this is too broad. The attribute is also emitted on nested helper classes and is not emitted on netstandard2.0/.NET Framework, so the claim and the guard text disagree on scope. Nothing in the diff documents a setting or an opt-out.

receipt_plan.detail: Compare the README sentence 'All generated formatters and resolvers are decorated' with the templates under Transforms/*.tt, which also decorate FormatterCache and GetFormatterHelper. The wording is imprecise but not wrong.

interpretations.label: A
interpretations.summary: Unconditionally emit [ExcludeFromCodeCoverage] on all generated types (formatters, resolvers, nested helpers), guarded by #if !NETSTANDARD2_0 && !NETFRAMEWORK, with no setting or opt-out. This is what the change implements.

interpretations.label: B
interpretations.summary: Emit the attribute by default but add an opt-out setting, for example a property on GeneratedMessagePackResolverAttribute or an MSBuild property read by the generator. The templates would check this option and omit the attribute when it is set. The requirement allows this ('setting would be fine to have too'). Optionally this reading could also add [GeneratedCode], or could emit a locally defined attribute on legacy targets.
